name: Fazio Giovanni Santori
summary:
Fazio Giovanni Santori was a prominent Italian Roman Catholic bishop and cardinal during the Renaissance.

Born in unknown year, he rose to prominence under Pope Leo X and was appointed Bishop of Siena in 1506. Santori played a key role in the Sack of Rome in 1527 and later became Archbishop of Bologna. He died on April 1, 1510, at the age of 63.

Santori's legacy includes his contributions to the Catholic Church during a tumultuous period in European history. He was known for his theological writings and his efforts to reform the Church's liturgical practices.

The legacy of Fazio Giovanni Santori can still be seen today in the many churches he helped build, including the impressive Santuario di San Francesco in Assisi.

As a cardinal, Santori participated in several conclave sessions, including one that elected Pope Clement VII.
